answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% and zero buffer, so deferral and a primary switch both raise delivery risk and are incompatible with the TCO-without-disruption objective. Incumbent continuity (c1) plus renewal-window commercial leverage (c4) and optional multi-year volume pricing (c6) is the only single action that can cut spend without a migration. Second-source (c3) does not replace the expiring primary this cycle; c2/c5 are not used because last year's cheap-vendor onboard and a non-critical month-to-month deferral do not transfer to this constraint set. Verifying c4 as the load-bearing claim that renewal renegotiation actually moves price. Whether recovered margin approaches the 18% mandate is unknown; avoid stretching payment terms that could deprioritize us. Downstream disruption risk is flagged given no buffer.
